# Blueprint

> Blueprint offers invited participants an initial evidence-backed assessment of one real task and a practical next step.

Blueprint offers a limited, invited beta for real sites and tasks. Share permitted video or discuss the work, describe the desired outcome, and provide feedback and follow-up. Invited participants receive a free initial evidence-backed assessment of what is supported, what is unknown, and a practical next step. Any later evaluation, integration, or physical pilot has its scope and cost agreed separately before proceeding. No guaranteed ready robot, instant automatic delivery, or free physical deployment. Simulation is not physical proof or a deployment guarantee.

## Public pages

- [Home](https://tryblueprint.io/)
- [How it works](https://tryblueprint.io/how-it-works)
- [Beta program](https://tryblueprint.io/beta)
- [Discuss your site](https://tryblueprint.io/contact/site-operator)
- [Robot teams: apply for early access](https://tryblueprint.io/contact/robot-team)
- [Privacy](https://tryblueprint.io/privacy)
- [Terms](https://tryblueprint.io/terms)

Robot teams register interest through the existing application. Applications remain pending until manual approval for a real site task; applying or creating an account does not grant access. Approved teams see only job cards sites chose to share. A task invitation does not guarantee a run, introduction, or deployment. Any later evaluation, integration, or physical pilot has its scope and cost agreed separately before proceeding. Private paid self-service evaluations and top-ups remain unavailable. Beta program: https://tryblueprint.io/beta. Contact: hello@tryblueprint.io.

## Evidence boundary

Customer wording uses “job” for the work a site wants automated and “task” for the specific robot action and its technical conditions. API fields and identifiers retain their existing names.

A Task Evaluation Run returns a decision or abstention. Pipeline owns method qualification and routing; physical outcomes remain distinct from simulation and generated evidence.

## Agent interfaces and compatibility

Current public/request tools are `blueprint.siteWorld.search`, `blueprint.catalog.search`, `blueprint.ask`, `blueprint.request.locationDraft`, `blueprint.siteWorld.get`, and `blueprint.siteWorld.launchReadiness`.

The historical read and hosted-session compatibility tools are `blueprint.commerce.order.get`, `blueprint.commerce.liveOrder.get`, `blueprint.commerce.entitlement.get`, `blueprint.commerce.entitlementReadiness`, `blueprint.session.create`, `blueprint.session.reset`, `blueprint.session.step`, `blueprint.session.runBatch`, `blueprint.session.control`, `blueprint.session.renderExplorer`, and `blueprint.session.export`. Historical availability does not make these current standalone products.

Team tools are `blueprint.team.me`, `blueprint.team.checkpoint.register`, `blueprint.team.checkpoint.list`, `blueprint.team.plan`, `blueprint.team.runs.start`, `blueprint.team.runs.release`, `blueprint.team.policy.get`, and `blueprint.team.policy.set`. Team account and checkpoint tools use a revocable per-team agent key bound to a verified Blueprint account. Early-access library admission remains required (403 `early_access_required` otherwise). During the invited beta, paid planning, dry-run purchase, run-start and top-up APIs return 403 `paid_evaluations_disabled`, including requests with `confirm: true`. Request an invited evaluation through the workspace. Execution requires operator approval of the exact team, policy, task, current rights, expiry, one attempt, and a separate Blueprint-funded compute limit. Historical balances and receipts remain available under their original access controls.

Truth labels are `capture_grounded`, `provider_derived`, `generated`, `request_gated`, `protected_robot_team`, `legacy_commerce_read_only`, and `decision_or_abstention`.
